newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down sharply on LME loss.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down sharply on LME loss.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down sharply on Monday due to panic selling after copper on the London Metal Exchange breached the $1,900 support level last Friday, traders said.
All later-maturing contracts fell below the key 20,000 yuan support level and the three-month contract hit a 1996 low.
The most active January 1997 contract ended at 19,840 yuan ($2,389) per tonne, losing 370 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 20,000 and hit a low of 19,800.
October fell 130 to 20,450 yuan, November 210 to 20,110, December 350 to 19,880, February 360 to 19,840, March 300 to 19,900 and April 330 to 19,950.
Combined volume rose sharply to 71,250 tonnes from 26,030.
Copper opened down and dropped further before most contracts closed near their intra-day lows.
Traders said that losses on the LME triggered panic selling and the outlook was for further falls since the key 20,000 yuan support had been breached.
"Stop loss selling and speculative selling were responsible for today's sharp falls," one trader said.
But some traders said that further sharp falls were unlikely unless the LME plunges again, because institutions had large long positions in hand.
"Institutions are likely to try to support future prices if there is no big negative news," a second trader said.
Most analysts said copper would fall further if the LME could not stand above $1,900 in the next few days.
Aluminium end most down. October was unchanged at 13,950 yuan, November fell 50 to 13,950 and December 100 to 13,900.
Combined volume rose to 1,400 tonnes from 300.
